lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

measurements.left_edges: col1 x64, col2 x432, all names share their column's edge: pass
measurements.baseline: 8 px grid, all 14 letter row tops mod 8 = 0; Spirits and Wine heads both at y608: pass. Phone row tops mod 8 = 1-3, so no baseline grid on the phone
measurements.header_levels: H2 DM Sans 600 13.5px gold .30em; H3 DM Sans 500 10.5px #B3B09E; one style per level: pass
measurements.section_gaps: 72 px between every pair of sections (Cocktails>Spirits, Beer>Cider, Cider>Wine), made of 40 px of padding per gap added to balance the columns, against an 8 px item gap
measurements.price_travel: 4% col1, 9% col2, 5% phone; inline, about 0.9 em hop; no row over 40%: pass
measurements.price_ink: prices #EFE6D2 weight 400 vs names #EFE6D2 weight 500: same ink, only 100 weight units apart, so 'Cognac VSOP 18' and 'Blanco Tequila 12' still read as age statements (brief section 5 violated)
measurements.contrast_on_ground_#10291F: ivory names/prices about 12.4:1; descriptions #C9C2AF about 8.7:1; gold heads #C8A765 about 6.7:1; sub-labels 7.08:1. Text keeps a 6 mm clearance from the art, so the worst pixel is the ground: pass
measurements.squint: 2 salient regions, primary/secondary 241, centroid (0.63, 0.59): the art dominates the lower right, not the wordmark
measurements.margins: left 64 px (16.9 mm); wordmark text box at top 64, but the cap tops sit at about 23 mm; text right edge 705 leaves 111 px (29 mm) before the art; declared bottom text end 808, then the field. Only the left and top margins are equal
measurements.bleed: art bbox 0-816 x 176-1056 = exactly trim, 0 mm bleed (need at least 3 mm): FAIL, so criterion 16 is capped at 40
measurements.description_measure: col2 is 170 px wide against col1's 336 px: an asymmetric measure

remove: The furrow strips (rays toward the vanishing point in strips 4, 6 and 8). They turn the field into op-art wave hatching that reads as ocean or Art Deco water, not Iowa strip-cropping, and they compete with the agave for the one-gesture slot. Keep only the contour-row strips.
top_problem: The idea does not read on the page. At arm's length this is ref-02 panel 3 (dark green, gold line agave, tracked CANTINA) with the cactus swapped for a faceted, sail-like agave and a wave field, so it fails the substitution test. The 'Iowa strip field' reads as generic engraved waves, and 'CANTINA' is the reference board's placeholder word, not an ownable wordmark. The boldest missing idea is to make the Mexico-Iowa fusion the structure itself (for example, the section grid laid out as the contour-strip plots, so the list sits in the field, with the agave as the single vertical interruption) instead of an illustration parked beside a generic list.
fixes: Add at least 3 mm of bleed to the art on the right and bottom edges (render the art canvas past trim and declare the trim and safe inset); until then criterion 16 stays capped at 40.

Make the field unmistakably agricultural and fuse it with the agave. Remove the furrow-ray strips, use straight-to-gently-curved contour rows with a strip-crop rhythm of alternating densities, and draw the agave's leaves as fleshy, channelled, rosette forms, not flat triangular blades that read as sails or crystal shards.
Set prices in the muted ink (#C9C2AF) or a visibly lighter weight so that 'Cognac VSOP 18', 'Blanco Tequila 12' and 'Añejo Tequila 16' cannot read as age statements.

Replace the 40 px padding gaps with a structural fix: widen col 2 to match col 1's measure, or pull the art higher so the columns end together naturally. The blank bands under the Brown Butter Old Fashioned and the Amber Lager are empty canvas, not whitespace.

Earn the wordmark. Either use the venue's real name, or give CANTINA one ownable move (for example, its baseline sitting on the field's horizon, or the agave cone crossing it) so the only large type and the one gesture interlock, rather than repeating ref-02 panel 3's centred tracked serif.

lens: items and prices vs draft_doc.json, ingredient completeness (public_components), menu flow
top_problem: Every item and price matches the draft: 14 items, 14 prices, nothing invented or dropped. The Manhattan's hidden aromatic bitters stay hidden, and the lime wheel, lime coin and orange peel garnishes trace to recipe_versions (cited in round-17). The menu underneath is still mostly empty: 10 of 14 descriptions just restate the item name ('Blanco tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Dry red wine', 'Toasty amber lager'). Beer has no ABV, wine has no grape-and-region line, and spirits have no brand. That is Rob's known data gap, not the designer's fault, but the page does not flag it. The flow is also broken up: to make both columns end at y 808, the designer padded the gaps, which leaves 72 px holes under Cocktails and under Draft Beer. Cider floats alone in a void, and Wine comes last, as an afterthought after Cider. The eye jumps between islands instead of following one path.
problems: Known data gap (Rob to fill, not the designer's fault): beer has no style+ABV, wine has no grape+region, spirits have no brand or age detail beyond the name. As a result, 10 of 14 descriptions only repeat the item name.
Brut Rosé 13 has no pour label (glass or bottle). 'By the Glass' covers Malbec and Pinot Grigio, but the Sparkling sub-head does not state a pour.

Column balance was bought with padded gaps: 72 px gaps plus 40 px extra per gap leave Cider stranded between two voids in col 2, and a dead band sits between Cocktails and Spirits in col 1. Grouping reads as islands, not a path.

Section order is Cocktails, Spirits, Draft Beer, Cider, Wine. Agave-first is defensible for a Mexican cantina. But the page reads as a two-column Z, so Spirits (bottom-left) and Wine (bottom-right) land on the same baseline and compete as parallel endpoints. Wine after Cider feels like leftover placement, not a deliberate sequence.

Margarita now comes before Manhattan in Classics, reversing the draft order. The content is unchanged, and leading a cantina with the Margarita is a good choice, but the change is not noted as an intentional reorder.
The House Daiquiri lost its draft 'house' qualifier on the demerara syrup, a small lost signal of house prep. Nothing was invented.

Prices are inline at the same size and colour as the names. The format is consistent (no $, whole numbers) and eye travel is short, but prices have no tabular rhythm down a section, so comparing prices means scanning a ragged line.
Wordmark 'CANTINA & Cocktail Bar' replaces the draft title 'Bar menu'. This is acceptable as a brand placeholder, but confirm the venue name with Rob before publishing.
fixes: Ask Rob for beer ABV and style, wine grape and region, and spirit brands. Until they arrive, drop the tautological descriptions for the unknown items and mark each one as missing_ingredients in the proposal, instead of printing 'Blanco tequila pour' or 'Dry red wine'.
Replace the padded 72 px + 40 px gaps with the standard section spacing. Let the columns end at different heights, or move Cider directly under Draft Beer with normal spacing so it stops floating.

Make the reading path explicit. Either run col 2 as Draft Beer, Cider, Wine at uniform spacing, or reorder to Cocktails, Spirits (agave), Wine, Beer, Cider, so the two bottom-aligned heads do not compete. State the order rationale in proposal.md.
Add a pour label to Brut Rosé (glass or bottle), or flag it as a missing input from Rob. Do not guess it.
Restore 'house demerara syrup' on the House Daiquiri, and log the Margarita-first reorder in proposal.md as an intentional change from the draft.

lens: Ingredient/garnish/label tracing to build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions (gateway log_id 220); description-price relationship in preview-letter.png
verified: Margarita 15: tequila blanco, fresh lime juice, orange liqueur, agave syrup come from draft components (menu_item 14555870). The lime wheel is recipe_versions f06abb74.garnish 'Lime wheel'. 'Bright and citrus-forward' is copied from the draft desc.

Manhattan 15: rye whiskey and sweet vermouth come from draft components. The cocktail cherry is recipe_versions 9fb77eaa.garnish 'Cocktail cherry' and also a draft component with role Garnish. Leaving out aromatic bitters is correct because meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false}.
House Daiquiri 14: white rum, fresh lime juice and demerara syrup come from draft components (menu_item 44dcba6e). The lime coin is recipe_versions 14d45e57.garnish 'Lime coin'.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16: brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara syrup and aromatic bitters come from draft components (menu_item 0cc4e912). The orange peel is recipe_versions 7095fd3d.garnish 'Orange peel'.
All 15 printed prices (7, 8, 7, 8, 12, 11, 13, 12, 16, 18, 15, 15, 14, 16) match phg.menu_items.menu_price and the draft prices.
Beer, cider, wine and spirits descriptions are copied word for word from the draft desc fields. 'Añejo' and 'Rosé' carry the correct accents.
No taglines or prop captions state an item fact: the only copy outside the items is '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa'.
phg.menu_items also has 'Junmai Ginjo' 12, which is not in the draft doc and is not printed. That is correct for this draft, but the Coordinator should confirm it was dropped on purpose.
top_problem: Every fact traces, but the copy is not guest language. Five of eleven non-cocktail descriptions just repeat the item name: 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Hop-forward draft IPA' and 'Dry sparkling cider'. The rest read like classes ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine'). Among the cocktails, only the Margarita gets a sensory sentence, and it is tacked onto a garnish ('lime wheel. Bright and citrus-forward.'), so the menu has two voices. It is a cantina where one of four cocktails is agave-based and the tequila pours carry no descriptor at all.
problems: Criterion 12: Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP, Dry-Hopped IPA and Dry Cider have descriptions that restate the name. Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé have taxonomy-style copy ('Dry red wine'). The source is draft desc text, which is still weak copy.
Criterion 12/10: the Margarita runs an ingredient list straight into a flavour sentence, while the Manhattan, Daiquiri and Old Fashioned are bare ingredient lists. Two voices on one page.

Criterion 13: for a Mexican cantina, agave is thin. It has one agave cocktail, two tequila pours and no mezcal or Mexican beer, and the draft beers are Czech Pilsner, IPA and Amber Lager. The data limits this, but the layout does not compensate: Spirits/Agave sits in the lower half of column 1 below the whiskey, rum and brandy content. 'CANTINA & Cocktail Bar' does not name the venue. The Iowa field art carries the city read; the copy carries none of it.
Criterion 14: Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Sparkling' with no glass or bottle label, while Malbec and Pinot Grigio inherit 'By the Glass'. The pour size is ambiguous to a guest.

Criterion 14: column 1 has a large empty band between the Old Fashioned (description ends at about y 1000 on the preview) and SPIRITS (about y 1165), and column 2 has one between Amber Lager and CIDER. The 72 px auto-gaps in the column-balancing read as dropped content rather than pacing. Prices sit inline and tight to their names (eye travel 4-9%), so association is clean.

Criterion 14: the column 2 measure is 170 px. Descriptions fit on one line now, but any real region, ABV or brand copy (the pending data gap) will wrap to 2-3 lines and collide with the agave's 6 mm clearance. The layout has no room reserved for the data Rob is filling in.
fixes: Replace the name-repeating spirit and beer descriptions with sourced guest language once Rob's region, ABV and brand data arrives. Until then, flag them missing_ingredients in the proposal and do not ship them as final copy.

Give all four cocktails the same pattern: either ingredients only, or ingredients plus one sourced sensory phrase. Move the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' to lead or trail consistently, not after the garnish.
Add a pour label for Brut Rosé (glass or bottle) from the draft or Rob. If none exists, list it as an open item and do not print it under a parent that implies 'By the Glass'.

Designer note: give agave more weight for a cantina, for example Spirits/Agave directly after Cocktails at the top of column 2 or a 'Tequila' head, and use the dead band in column 1 instead of auto-gaps.
Designer note: widen column 2 or let it run to 2-line descriptions now, so the pending ABV, region and brand text fits without re-flowing into the agave clearance.
